summary:
The Isle of Man is a self-legislating Crown Dependency. Tynwald enacts its own statutes on gender recognition, equality and criminal law, and United Kingdom legislation reaches the island only when extended by Order in Council rather than automatically.

The Gender Recognition Act 2009 (c.11) allows transgender people to change their legal gender and to have the new gender recognised.

The Equality Act 2017, which received royal assent on 18 July 2017 and was largely in force from 1 January 2019, lists gender reassignment as a protected characteristic and as a ground on which discrimination is prohibited. The same Act lists sexual orientation as a protected characteristic, defined to include attraction to the same, opposite or either sex and lack of attraction to either sex.

A ban on conversion therapy covering both sexual orientation and gender identity was passed in 2020 as an amendment to the sexual offences bill in the Legislative Council and took effect in 2024. In 2024 the Isle of Man became the first British territory, and the first part of the British Isles, to ban conversion therapy.

In July 2022 community consultation progressed on a hate crime bill that would explicitly include gender reassignment alongside sexual orientation and marital or civil partnership status.

Same-sex marriage took effect on 22 July 2016 after royal assent on 19 July 2016 for the Marriage and Civil Partnership Act. Civil partnerships have been available since 6 April 2011 under the Civil Partnership Act 2011 (c.2), and the first conversion of a civil partnership to a marriage was completed within days of the 2016 Act taking effect, with conversion possible without a second ceremony.

Under the Employment Act 2006 (c.21), effective 1 September 2006, dismissal on grounds of sexual orientation was unlawful. The House of Keys had adopted a sexual-orientation employment protection amendment on 30 November 2005.

Isle of Man Prison (Jurby), the island's only functioning prison, opened fully on 14 August 2008 and holds separate units for remand and convicted prisoners, female prisoners, young offenders, vulnerable prisoners and a segregation unit. No birth-sex-versus-identity placement rule, no trans-specific unit, and no trans-specific solitary or segregation practice are documented in this record.

Private and consensual male homosexual acts were decriminalised in September 1992 with an age of consent of 21, lowered to 18 by the Criminal Justice Act 2001 (c.4), then lowered to 16 and made gender-neutral by the Sexual Offences (Amendment) Act 2006 (c.3). Until 2021, Section 9 of the Sexual Offences Act 1992 retained offences of buggery and gross indecency between men if under 16 or committed other than in private; in 2021 the more-than-two-persons specification was deleted and language on indecent exposure and sexual activity in a public place was made gender-neutral.

The Sexual Offences and Obscene Publications Act 2021 received royal assent in July 2021 and took effect on 1 July 2022, pardoning historical gay sex offences committed before 1992 on the model of the United Kingdom's 2017 Alan Turing law. Chief Minister Howard Quayle issued an unqualified apology to gay men convicted under previous laws, and in August 2022 the police commissioner formally apologised for enforcement of anti-gay laws up to 1992.

Same-sex couples have had equal access to full joint or stepchild adoption since 6 April 2011 under the Civil Partnership Act 2011, and lesbian couples have access to artificial insemination. As of an August 2023 consultation, same-sex couples were not recognised as parents on birth certificates from IVF and surrogacy, and no laws acknowledge surrogacy.
tangentialFactors:
The 2016 marriage reform was preceded by public political backing: Chief Minister Allan Bell stated on 9 June 2015 that he would formulate a bill to repeal the island's marriage prohibition.

The 2005 employment amendment was tabled by Onchan MHK Peter Karran and aligned the island with United Kingdom human-rights law on sexual-orientation non-discrimination.

The conversion-therapy ban's passage as an amendment to a broader sexual offences bill, rather than as standalone legislation, means its operative text sits within the sexual offences framework rather than the Equality Act 2017.

The hate crime bill covering gender reassignment was at community-consultation stage in July 2022; this record does not document its subsequent enactment or commencement.
localsOnly:
Local residents can change their legal gender under the Gender Recognition Act 2009 (c.11) and are protected against discrimination on grounds of gender reassignment under the Equality Act 2017.

Residents in civil partnerships since 6 April 2011 can convert to marriage without a second ceremony following the Marriage and Civil Partnership Act's entry into force on 22 July 2016.

Gay men convicted of historical offences before 1992 are eligible for a pardon under the Sexual Offences and Obscene Publications Act 2021, which took effect 1 July 2022; Chief Minister Howard Quayle and, in August 2022, the police commissioner issued formal apologies for those convictions and their enforcement.

Isle of Man Prison (Jurby) is the island's only functioning prison, a GBP 41.7m facility at the former RAF Jurby base, fully operational from 14 August 2008 and run by the Isle of Man Prison Service, with separate units for remand and convicted prisoners, female prisoners, young offenders, vulnerable prisoners and a segregation unit.
outOfScopeNotes:
No entry, visa or border-screening rules specific to transgender travellers are documented in this record; the island's immigration arrangements stand under the United Kingdom framework and are not sourced here.

No trans-specific violence statistics, homicide counts or survey prevalence figures for transgender residents are documented in this record, so no comparison against the island's general homicide rate can be drawn.

The hate crime bill that would explicitly include gender reassignment was at community-consultation stage in July 2022; its enactment, commencement and current status are unresolved in this record.

Whether the Equality Act 2017's gender-reassignment protection extends to prisoners at Jurby, and whether any policy governs housing by birth sex versus gender identity, is unresolved: the record documents the prison's unit structure but no trans-specific placement rule.

Birth-certificate parentage for same-sex couples arising from IVF and surrogacy was unresolved as of an August 2023 consultation; later developments are not sourced here.
